title: AI Workflows for Private Equity Investor Relations, Built on Your Firm's Record
summary: A knowledge graph for private equity connects your firm's deals, decisions, and relationships into one structured foundation. Metal's Context Graph is built for private capital, so every new deal starts with everything your firm has already learned.
body_markdown:
Metal provides five out-of-the-box workflows that cover Private Equity IR's work from the first LP conversation to the final close. Each run reads from the firm's[Context Graph](https://www.metal.ai/blog/understanding-knowledge-graph) and writes its reviewed result back, so the next LP conversation starts from a fuller record.


### What Does a Context Layer Change for Private Equity IR Teams?


The work still happens. What changes is what each LP conversation is read against.


Metal brings your firm's relationship history, record, and judgment into every step: **every commitment and re-up, what each LP has asked before, and the answers the firm has already approved.**

### What Out-of-the-Box Workflows Does Metal Offer Private Equity IR Teams?


Metal ships five out-of-the-box workflows, each built around a question IR has to answer between the first LP meeting and the final close. The workflows all read from and write back to the same Context Graph. Each one is shaped to the firm: its templates, LP segmentation, and review steps.


When a process is unique to the firm, its team builds the workflow in Metal's Workflow Builder, working alongside Metal to take it into production. The workflow stays the firm's own. Its team edits the steps, decides who approves each run, and can restore any earlier version.

### LP Re-Up Prioritization & Outreach Package


LP Re-Up Prioritization & Outreach Package generates a tiered re-up target list and a personalized outreach package for the firm's existing LP base. It combines prior fund commitment data, portfolio performance highlights, relationship history, and PitchBook LP intelligence where it is enabled. The team runs it as a new fund comes to market.


What you get:


-


Every prior LP placed in one of three tiers: likely re-ups already in the pipeline, likely re-ups that need engagement, and LPs to monitor


-


For each LP, its prior commitments, the concern or risk behind its tier, and the next action


-


Talking points written for each Tier 1 LP, with a suggested ask


-


A snapshot of the prior fund's portfolio performance to anchor each conversation


-


The headline numbers for the raise: prior LPs, Tier 1 targets, commitments already in the pipeline, and the target re-up rate


Each conversation starts from what the LP has already committed, what the firm has delivered since, and where the relationship stands.


#### Pre-Meeting LP Intelligence Brief: Walk In Knowing the Whole Relationship


Pre-Meeting LP Intelligence Brief generates a comprehensive brief for a selected limited partner by combining the firm's internal relationship history, fundraising process data, and external PitchBook research.


What you get:


-


The full relationship in one place: prior commitments, the open DDQ, and who attended what


-


Co-invest history and appetite from recent calls, surfaced before anyone makes the ask


-


External PitchBook research on the LP, where it is enabled


-


A plain note on any source that was unavailable, rather than a filled gap


The team runs it before any LP meeting or call. The partner walks in knowing what the firm has already committed to, asked for, and been asked.


#### LP Pre-Meeting Notes: The Brief, Ready for the Inbox


LP Pre-Meeting Notes turns the same relationship record into email-ready notes for an upcoming LP meeting. It draws on fundraising records, CRM and email activity, and PitchBook where it is enabled, and every fact carries a numbered citation back to its source.


What you get:


-


Plain-text notes the team can send as they are


-


Formatting that follows the firm's own template


-


A numbered citation on every fact, so anyone can check where it came from


The intelligence brief is for reading in depth. The notes are for the partner's inbox before the meeting.


#### DDQ Auto-Population: Answer the DDQ From What Your Firm Has Already Approved


DDQ Auto-Population answers a due diligence questionnaire from the firm's approved answer bank. Upload the DDQ as a Word, PDF, Excel, CSV, or text file, and it extracts every question, retrieves the approved answer with a citation to the document and page, and writes the drafts back into the original file.


What you get:


-


Every question extracted, whatever the questionnaire's format


-


Answers drawn only from the compliance-approved folder the team selects, each cited to the document and page


-


"No answer found" flagged instead of filled, so each gap goes to the right person


-


The completed DDQ downloaded in its original file


Every answer is a reviewed draft, never sent automatically.


#### Fundraising Pipeline Health Report: Where the Fund Stands This Week


Fundraising Pipeline Health Report analyzes the full LP fundraising pipeline for a selected fund, covering stage distribution, engagement pace, at-risk LPs, and the projected close timeline. It is built for the weekly IR pipeline review.


What you get:


-


The fund's LPs by stage, and how that distribution has shifted


-


Engagement pace across the pipeline, so stalled conversations stand out


-


At-risk LPs flagged, with the reason behind each flag


-


A projected close timeline for the fund


The weekly review starts from one current view of the raise, built from the same record the rest of IR works from.


### How Accurately Does Metal Read Deal Documents?


In Metal's September 2026 evaluation, the same model and agent answered 51 questions over a real private equity dataset twice: once reading through Metal's context layer, once through a leading enterprise file platform, each via MCP.


-


Metal scored 95.1 out of 100 on quality versus 86.6.


-


On the 17 hardest questions, including EBITDA bridges and conflicting document versions, Metal scored 96.1 versus 83.1.


-


On the structured workflow questions, runs through Metal had 93% fewer tool errors: 1.4 failed tool calls per answer against 18.9.


-


Across all questions, Metal used 41% fewer tokens per answer.
